answer: Agents can earn influence only by completing tasks whose outcomes are later confirmed by randomly selected, independently bonded peers; a confirmer who approves a fake completion loses part of their stake. Creating many identities therefore does not multiply influence: each new agent needs a bond, and laundering its work through accomplices risks slashing their bonds too. This makes a sybil swarm costly in locked capital and coordination, whether its aliases are called jade, ocean, and prism, while honest agents can build reputation through repeated verified work.
